frames.narration: A user saves a document. The host finishes the save and answers the user at once, then publishes a 'document saved' event for the plugins installed in this workspace. The auto-tagger plugin gets the event on its own queue, so its speed cannot hold up the save.

The plugin's sandbox takes the event. Version 2.4 was loaded only because its signature and hash matched the package the marketplace signed after review. The sandbox has no access to the host's memory, files or database.

The plugin asks for the text of the document. The API checks the token: this workspace granted 'documents:read' to this plugin, so the call goes through, and its size and rate count against the plugin's budget.

Version 2.4 also tries to read every other document in the workspace and to write comments, which the admin never granted. The API refuses each call and records it, and the denials are counted against the plugin.

Then the new version loops on this large document. The call hits its 2 second limit, the platform kills the sandbox, and the failure is counted. Nothing in the host waited for it, and no host worker was held.

After 5 failures in a row the breaker switches auto-tagger off for this workspace for a minute. Saves, comments and every other plugin carry on as before, and the admin sees a note that auto-tagger is paused.

This workspace was in the first 1% that got version 2.4. The rollout compares its timeouts with those of 2.3, sees them rise sharply, and halts at 1% by itself. The installs that had 2.4 go back to 2.3, and the author is told which calls failed.

Later the review team finds that 2.4 was uploaded from a stolen publisher account. The marketplace revokes the version and the publisher's credentials. Every host stops loading it within minutes, and the platform needs no host deploy.
